The '''2010–11 [[Cypriot First Division]]''' was the 72nd season of the [[Cyprus|Cypriot]] top-level [[Association football|football]] league. It began on 27 August 2010 with the first matches of the [[#First round|first round]] and will end on 11 May 2011 with the last matches of the [[#Second round|second round]]. The defending champions were [[AC Omonia|Omonia]]. [[APOEL FC|APOEL]] won the championship four matchweeks before the end of the season.

==Competition modus==
Fourteen teams participate in the competition. Eleven of them have also competed in the [[2009–10 Cypriot First Division|2009–10 season]] while the remaining three teams were promoted from the [[Cypriot Second Division|Second Division]].

Each team plays against every other team twice, once at home and once away, for a total of 26 matches. After these matches, the two teams with the worst records will be relegated to the Second Division. The remaining twelve teams will be divided into three groups of four teams each.

The teams ranked first through fourth will play for the championship and to participate in the European competitions. Teams ranked ninth through 12th will determine the third relegated club, while the remaining four teams will play a placement round. Every team plays twice against its group opponents. Regular season records are carried over without any modifications.

==Teams==
[[Nea Salamis Famagusta FC|Nea Salamis Famagusta]] and [[APEP Pitsilia]] were relegated at the end of the first stage of the [[2009–10 Cypriot First Division|2009–10 season]] after finishing in the bottom two places of the table. They were joined by [[Aris Limassol FC|Aris Limassol]], who finished at the bottom of the second-phase Group C.

The relegated teams were replaced by [[2009–10 Cypriot Second Division|2009–10 Second Division]] champions [[Alki Larnaca FC|Alki Larnaca]], runners-up [[AEK Larnaca]] and third-placed team [[Olympiakos Nicosia]].
